Using only the stated functors, the natural endomorphism algebra of  
\(P(V)=V\oplus \operatorname{Sym}^2(V)\) is
\[
\left\{\begin{pmatrix}a&0\\ b&d\end{pmatrix}:a,b,d\in\mathbb F_2\right\},
\]
where \(b\) is the natural square map \(v\mapsto v^2\). Hence a natural endomorphism \(E:F\to F\), with \(F=P^{\oplus 5}\), has the form
\[
E=\begin{pmatrix}A&0\\ B&D\end{pmatrix},
\qquad A,B,D\in M_5(\mathbb F_2).
\]
It is idempotent iff
\[
A^2=A,\qquad D^2=D,\qquad DB+BA=B.
\]
Also
\[
C_E=E\Pi-\Pi E=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\ B&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For \(V=\mathbb F_2^n\), the square map \(V\to \operatorname{Sym}^2(V)\) is injective, so
\[
\operatorname{rank}(C_E)_V=n\,\operatorname{rank}(B).
\]

Let \(a=\operatorname{rank}A\), \(d=\operatorname{rank}D\). The equation \(DB+BA=B\) says
\[
B(\operatorname{im}A)\subseteq \ker D,\qquad B(\ker A)\subseteq \operatorname{im}D.
\]
Thus
\[
\operatorname{rank}B\le \min(a,5-d)+\min(5-a,d).
\]
The maximum is \(5\), attained exactly when \(a+d=5\). The second largest possible rank is \(4\).

The number of rank-\(a\) idempotents in \(M_5(\mathbb F_2)\) is
\[
I_a=\binom 5a_2 2^{a(5-a)},
\]
so
\[
(I_0,I_1,I_2,I_3,I_4,I_5)=(1,496,9920,9920,496,1).
\]
Counting the allowed \(B\)’s gives
\[
N_n^{(1)}=208326666240,
\]
and the rank-\(4\) count gives
\[
N_n^{(2)}=1170523831680.
\]

Therefore, for every \(n\ge2\),
\[
\boxed{
\left(R_n^{(1)},N_n^{(1)},R_n^{(2)},N_n^{(2)}\right)
=
\left(5n,\ 208326666240,\ 4n,\ 1170523831680\right).
}
\]
